patch.value: Consume the canonical attestation gate instead of carrying a copy of it

This repository carried its own 689-line shell scanner and 500-line verifier, duplicated from the same origin as every other package in the fleet. That gate decides whether an artefact may reach the registry, so a false pass is the failure that matters - and the canonical implementation has had many fail-open constructions found and closed in it. A copy frozen at any point in that sequence still admits every construction closed after it. The scanner is deleted, the verifier becomes a thin launcher over the published pm-ops/attestation export. Measured BEFORE: 11 wrong. Measured AFTER (target): nonliteral-overwrite,nonliteral-overwrite-cmdsub.

Delete scripts/shell-command-scan.ts; Rewrite scripts/verify-release-publish-attestation.ts as a thin launcher over pm-ops/attestation; Replace test/shell-command-scan.test.ts and test/verify-release-publish-attestation.test.ts as consumer tests; All quality gates pass: check, docstring, coverage, verify:release-publish-attestation, test

value.text:
Greptile found that the convergence guard did not actually guard. The test asserted that the symbols imported from pm-ops/attestation are functions, and its own comment claimed they were the launcher's functions by reference - but it never compared the two. A launcher that imports the package and then re-exports a local wrapper would have passed, which is exactly the re-fork the test exists to catch.

The test now imports the launcher's own bindings and asserts reference equality against the package's. Proven not vacuous: replacing the re-export with a local arrow wrapper that still calls through to the package makes the test fail, and restoring it makes it pass.

message: review round: the convergence guard did not guard

CORRECTION to the acceptance record in this item. The comment above and the close reason record 'AFTER: clean (0 wrong)'. That measurement is FALSE for what this branch ships: it was taken through pm-ops pinned to file:../../../../../../tmp/pm-ops-2026.9.6-1/... - a tarball built from an unmerged working tree - so it measured a different system than the one being shipped.

Measured again against the published pm-ops@2026.9.7 that this branch now depends on, the corpus reads: nonliteral-overwrite, nonliteral-overwrite-cmdsub, quoted-metachar-value, single-quoted-metachar-value, multiword-unreadable-tail, quoted-paren-in-substitution, unterminated-substitution. Seven cases, every one of them open in the canonical implementation itself rather than in this repository, and every one closed by unbraind/pm-ops#100. They close here with an ordinary version bump.

So the honest statement of what this branch achieves is: 11 wrong -> 7 wrong, and the 7 are now shared with every other converged repository instead of being this repository's own. That is the value of convergence - not that the count reaches zero today, but that one release moves it everywhere.

Found by Greptile on review. The record mattering here is not cosmetic: the changelog is generated from these items, so a false clean claim would have shipped as a security claim.
